Hi Alex / Priya —

Thanks again for the time this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we all have alignment: 

- Scope: 3-week pilot, 2 hosted inference routes, single-tenant data isolation, SOC2 + limited data retention.
- Primary success criteria: end-to-end latency < 300ms P95 and cost per 1k tokens under target.
- Technical owners: Dev Patel (solutions) will own the integration + initial runbook.

Legal / procurement follow-ups we need to map out:
1) Economic buyer: who will sign the order?
2) NDA ownership: who should receive our NDA (attached)?
3) MSA/DPA routing: who owns redlines (legal), who fields DPA details (privacy/compliance)?
4) Estimated review times from legal/procurement so we can set a pilot start date.

Attachments: Redwood_NDA_v2.pdf (attached) — this is our standard mutual NDA; happy to send via DocuSign if that helps.

Proposed next steps:
- Alex: can you confirm the economic buyer and legal/procurement contacts (name/email) and preferred sequencing (NDA first vs. MSA + DPA together)?
- Dev: I’ll share the MSA initial redline once Alex confirms contacts.
- Sean: FYI and available to escalate if we need compressed SLAs on legal turn times.

Goal: get NDA signed and kickoff security questionnaire by end of next week so we can aim for pilot start the week after.

Thanks —
Marissa

Thanks Marissa — quick technical notes to add for legal: 
- The DPA is usually a short addendum that lists subprocessors (we use AWS/GCP), data retention windows, and encryption at rest/in transit details. We can pre-populate a DPA draft to speed review.
- Security questionnaire (self-attestation + evidence) will be required; we can provide SOC2 report and a short network diagram.
- For sequencing, our recommended flow is NDA (if requested) -> Security questionnaire -> MSA redline -> DPA finalization. This avoids blocking technical evidence requests behind MSA redlines.

I’ll draft the MSA initial redline once Alex confirms the legal contact.

- Dev
